name: Lotos Salad With Rich Sesame Sauce
author: Craig Claiborne, Pierre Franey

ingredients.raw: 2 unskinned, unboned whole chicken breasts, about 1 ½ to 1 ¾ pounds
ingredients.preparation: unboned whole chicken breasts, about 1 ½ to 1 ¾ pounds

ingredients.raw: 2 red peppers (sweet green peppers may be substituted), cored, seeded and cut into thin strips, about two cups
ingredients.item: red peppers (sweet green peppers may be substituted)
ingredients.preparation: cored, seeded and cut into thin strips, about two cups

ingredients.raw: 2 cups shredded roast pork (purchased or homemade)
1 tablespoon corn, peanut or vegetable oil
½ cup chopped fresh coriander leaves

steps.text: Bring enough water to the boil to cover the chicken breasts when added. Cut the breasts in half and add them to the water. When the water returns to the boil, cover and let simmer six minutes. Remove from the heat and let stand 15 minutes.

Remove the chicken pieces and plunge them into a basin of water with ice cubes. Let stand 15 minutes. Remove the chicken and pat dry. It is now ready to be used. Or it may be wrapped closely in plastic wrap and refrigerated overnight. You may also prepare the remaining ingredients and store them tightly covered in the refrigerator. When ready to serve, blend the foods.

You may use the bean sprouts as they are purchased. It is more refined, however, if you pull off the curlicues and seed portions of each. There should be four cups plucked-over sprouts. Put the sprouts in a mixing bowl.
Cut the cucumbers lengthwise into strips. Cut the strips into spaghetti-like shreds. There should be about four cups. Add them to the mixing bowl.
Cut the peppers into thin strips and shred the pork. Add them to the mixing bowl.
Remove and discard the skin and bones of the chicken breasts. Shred the meat. There should be about three cups. Add this to the bowl.

Drop the noodles into a large quantity of boiling water. Cook four minutes. Drain well and rinse under cold water until chilled. Drain once more. Cut into shreds of manageable length and put the noodles into a second bowl. Add the corn oil and sesame oil. Chill.
Combine the noodles and the pork, chicken and vegetable mixture. Add the sesame sauce and toss. Add the coriander and blend. Serve immediately.

name: London Fog Cookies
author: Carolina Gelen
description: These oversized cookies capture the essence of a frothy, bergamot-scented London Fog tea latte in every crumb. Start by infusing melted butter with a generous amount of Earl Grey tea and, if you like, culinary lavender, creating a flavor-packed foundation for the cookie dough. For a perfectly crisp exterior and a chewy, fudgy interior, bake the cookies until lightly golden and fragrant, with centers that still look a bit underbaked. Finish by topping the cookies with a delicate layer of milky, butter-laced vanilla frosting to mimic the vanilla foam floating on top of a London Fog.

ingredients.raw: 3 Earl Grey teabags (or 1 ½ tablespoons/6 grams tea leaves)
ingredients.item: earl grey teabags (or 1 ½ tablespoons/6 grams tea leaves)

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon culinary lavender, optional (see Tip), plus more for decorating
ingredients.preparation: optional (see Tip), plus more for decorating

ingredients.raw: ½ cup plus 2 tablespoons/116 grams granulated sugar
½ packed cup/100 grams light brown sugar
ingredients.item: packed cup/100 grams light brown sugar

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon kosher salt, such as Diamond Crystal

steps.text: In a small saucepan over medium heat, add the butter. Once the butter is mostly melted, cut open the teabags, add the tea and stir for a minute. Add the lavender, if using, then remove the pot from heat. Steep, covered, for 10 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, combine the granulated sugar, brown sugar, vanilla and salt. To a small bowl, add the flour, baking powder and baking soda and whisk to combine.

Pour the tea-infused butter over the sugar. Using a silicone spatula, vigorously stir to combine. Make sure the batter is not sizzling hot, then add the egg and vigorously stir for 1 to 2 minutes to combine while cooling down the batter. Add the dry ingredients and mix until there are no dry flour spots. Chill the cookie dough uncovered for 10 minutes in the fridge.

When ready to bake, divide the dough into eight ¼-cup balls (a 4-tablespoon scoop is helpful here) and place on the small sheet pan (you should have 8 balls, each weighing about 80 grams). Transfer the cookie balls to a small parchment-lined sheet pan or a large plate and freeze for 45 minutes, uncovered, until firm to the touch.

Arrange racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven. Heat the oven to 350 degrees. Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper. Arrange half of the frozen cookie dough on each sheet, leaving 5 inches between each cookie.

Bake for about 16 minutes, until the cookies look lightly golden and puffed up, while the centers still look a bit underbaked. Firmly knock the bottom of the pans against a hard heat-proof surface a few times to flatten the cookies. Cool for 5 minutes, then transfer the cookies to a cooling rack to cool completely.
In a microwave-safe bowl, microwave the butter for about 30 seconds, until very soft but not completely melted. Add the sugar, milk, vanilla and a tiny pinch of salt. Whisk until smooth.

Drizzle one or two thick stripes of frosting on each room-temperature cookie using a silicone spatula. Decorate with more lavender if you like. The glaze will take a moment to set and will maintain a softer consistency, so it’s better if the cookies are not stacked right away. Store in an airtight container or zip-close bag for up to 2 days.
